production.note: US model year 2016 only. KBB lists "R Coupe 2D" for 2016 (kbb-911-2016-specs) and no R trim for 2017 (kbb-911-2017-specs); KBB's news story (kbb-news-911-r-2016) calls it the 2016 Porsche 911 R with "deliveries slated to begin in the U.S. by late summer". Porsche: "Porsche will be building a total of only 991 units of the 911 R" (porsche-newsroom-911-r-geneva).

displacementL.note: 3,996 cc. Porsche AG Geneva 2016 press kit technical data: "3,996 cm³" displacement.

fuel.note: Petrol engine (NEDC consumption quoted in l/100 km); inferred.

drivetrain.note: Rear-engined, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description (no all-wheel-drive system mentioned).

transmission.note: "six-speed manual transmission"; no PDK was offered.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL: US rating from a single named-author article, with an unsigned article and a database agreeing. Quote (KBB news, Matt DeLorenzo, 1 March 2016): "the 3.8-liter boxer engine produces 500 horsepower" (the article's "3.8-liter" is wrong: the engine is 3,996 cc, see displacement). The Detroit Bureau (no byline): "500 horsepower 4.0-liter naturally aspirated flat-six engine" (detroitbureau-911-r-2016); KBB specs (database): "500 @ 8250 RPM" (kbb-911-2016-specs). Porsche AG's release gives "368 kW (500 hp ...)" (porsche-newsroom-911-r-geneva), where "hp" means PS (500 PS = 493 hp), so it is not the US rating and is not used for the value.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: a single named-author article for the US figure, with unsigned and database corroboration. Quote (KBB news, Matt DeLorenzo, 1 March 2016): "tipping the scales at just 3,021 lbs". The Detroit Bureau (no byline): "curb weight of just 3,021 pounds" (detroitbureau-911-r-2016); KBB specs (database): "3021 pounds" (kbb-911-2016-specs). Porsche AG's figure agrees: "With its overall weight of 1,370 kilograms, the 911 R undercuts the 911 GT3 RS by 50 kilograms." (porsche-geneva-2016-press-kit; 1,370 kg = 3,020 lb), a European DIN figure. Coupe, 6-speed manual, the only configuration.

sources.title: Porsche 911 R: successful model at the Geneva Motor Show
2016 Porsche 911 R: limited numbers, race-ready (Matt DeLorenzo, 1 March 2016)

provisionalNote: Power and weight are provisional. Power (500 hp, US) rests on one named-author article (KBB news, Matt DeLorenzo), with The Detroit Bureau (no byline) and KBB's spec table agreeing; Porsche AG's '500 hp' is a PS figure. Weight (3,021 lb) rests on the same KBB news article, corroborated by The Detroit Bureau and KBB's spec table, and consistent with Porsche AG's 1,370 kg. A Porsche Cars North America press release or spec sheet for the 2016 911 R, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend spec panel, would replace both.
